title: The West Country's 'most haunted' pubs and hotels where guests cannot explain encounters
excerpt: Ahead of Halloween, we have compiled some of the most popular haunted stories in pubs and hotels.
content:
The Shoemakers Museum in Street, Somerset, is housed in a 16th Century manor called the Grange.

According to Sam Cullen, manager at the museum, the site is "super-duper haunted".

She said the memoir Tales of the Polden Hills, by Frances Wood, written in 1922, describes supernatural occurrences.

"This was during a time when people loved a ghost story, when the unknown and creepy was exciting for folk," Cullen said.

She said one of the stories tells of two brothers who lived in the manor, one of whom reported seeing a white dog in the kitchen.

"A few moments later the other brother came running in and told the exact same tale," Cullen said.

"The only difference was that in this retelling the dog got up and left the room via the door. And the boy was like, 'how did the dog leave, the door was locked?'

"Within three weeks their father died in his study."

Cullen said when she started working at the museum, she did not know about the history.

"I thought it was just an abandoned old building," she said.

"All of the sudden, this disinfectant hospital smell came out of nowhere," she added.

"I asked, 'why does it smells like hospitals in the barn?'

"It turns out it used to be used as a quarantine hospital during the Spanish flu," she added.
